original_question: For a closed set C subset of R, the paper states that I(C) is arithmetic, specifically Sigma^0_2. What is the complexity of the set of Sigma^0_2 formulas phi such that phi defines I(C) for some closed set C, and in particular is this set Sigma^1_2-complete?
target_in_paper: Section 1 (Theodore Slaman), Problem 1(2), p. 2: the complexity of the collection of Σ^0_2 definitions that arise as I(C) for some closed set C⊆ℝ.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact target as the second subquestion of Problem 1 in Section 1: it keeps the restriction to closed C⊆ℝ, correctly notes that I(C) is arithmetic (indeed Σ^0_2), asks for the complexity of the set of Σ^0_2 formulas defining some I(C), and includes the paper’s specific follow-up question of whether that set is Σ^1_2-complete.
missing_details: The paper first defines I(A) for arbitrary A⊆ℝ by I(A) = {f : f is a gauge function and H^f(A) > 0}; this definition needs to be stated explicitly for the question to stand alone.
The symbol H^f denotes the Hausdorff measure associated with the gauge function f; the draft assumes this notation without defining it.
The complexity question is about the set of codes/Gödel numbers of Σ^0_2 arithmetic formulas, not formulas viewed only informally.
To say that a formula φ ‘defines I(C)’ one must fix a standard effective coding of gauge functions and require that φ define exactly the coded set I(C).
The paper explicitly records the existing lower bound ‘It is Π^1_1-hard,’ which is useful context and should be retained.
The paper’s wording only gives the ambient space through the earlier line ‘Given A⊆ℝ’; the refined version should restate that C is a closed subset of ℝ.

The paper does not spell out whether parameters are allowed in the Σ^0_2 formulas or which coding of formulas/gauge functions is used, so a stand-alone formulation should say that these are fixed by a standard coding convention.
refined_question: Fix a standard effective coding of gauge functions and of arithmetic formulas. For A⊆ℝ, let I(A) = {f : f is a gauge function and H^f(A) > 0}, where H^f is the Hausdorff measure associated with f. It is known that for every closed set C⊆ℝ, the set I(C) is arithmetic, in fact Σ^0_2. What is the lightface descriptive complexity of the set S of Gödel codes of Σ^0_2 arithmetic formulas φ such that φ defines, under the chosen coding, exactly I(C) for some closed set C⊆ℝ? The paper notes that S is already Π^1_1-hard; in particular, is S Σ^1_2-complete?
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper. In Section 1, Theodore Slaman first defines I(A)= {f gauge function : H^f(A)>0} and then, in Problem 1(2), asks essentially the same question as your draft: for closed C, since I(C) is arithmetic (Σ^0_2), what is the complexity of the set of Σ^0_2 formulas that define some I(C), and is that set Σ^1_2-complete? The only sharpening needed to make your draft fully stand-alone is to restore the definition of I(A), make explicit that formulas are considered via codes, and specify that ‘defines I(C)’ means equality with the coded set I(C) for some closed C⊆ℝ.
